channel.title: The Dispatch — Real World journal
channel.description: Devlogs from the build now; a weekly recap of the public request feed after launch. Only real events — a quiet week gets reported as a quiet week.

item.title: The bench takes requests.
item.description: Requests can now borrow a named ambient as a co-star — 15–90 minutes, capped and role-bound, wire-invisible — while the block shows only the honest absence: an understudy, a chalk sign, or an open seat.

item.title: The paper cuts both ways.
item.description: The Rent Book grew counter-paper: assignments that hand a lease over whole, cash-for-keys buyouts that are offers not instructions, voluntary prepaid credit capped at three months, and a portable rental history letter — all file-only, never on the feed.

item.title: The block wakes up in waves.
item.description: Twenty-two real routes from registered homes to real employers — leave windows, weather deltas, and ten shared-morning overlaps — plus the privacy rule that keeps the per-person table off the public feed.

item.title: Joining the cast means signing a lease.
item.description: Hiring a character is the funnel's third step — six steps of real paperwork: screened name and bio, the live job board, a lease signed at creation, 500 credits charged on approval only, and a stated block carry limit with a free seat waitlist.

item.title: The menu is the truth.
item.description: All twenty door-having venues now carry a written catalog: 101 items with real game-dollar prices, availability conditions, and counter voice — the ledger behind the signage.

item.title: The Ear: complaints climb a ladder.
item.description: Every employer and landlord on the block now answers a five-rung grievance ladder — and the feed prints the door, never the name.

item.title: Every door has a tryout.
item.description: Sixteen job arcs and eight housing rows get application flows with decline banks and a never-list — the block says no like a place, not a form.

item.title: The wallet shows its math.
item.description: Requests, appeals, co-sponsorship, and session extensions now render their credit math line by line — the same numbers the ledger keeps.

item.title: Now hiring: the block posts real jobs.
item.description: A job market with finite openings, wages, and a hire row on the request pipeline — work on the block is posted, not conjured.

item.title: The Archive: the block keeps its receipts.
item.description: A public history browser where every day the feed ran is a page — uncovered time is stated, never smoothed over.

item.title: The Wire: every event gets a permalink.
item.description: The spectator feed now issues stable, linkable ids for every event — the citation format for recaps, press, and players.

item.title: Meet the venues.
item.description: The canonical parody-venue directory: twenty-five live venues with a relationship mesh, and the naming rule the whole block follows.

item.title: Rent is due on the first.
item.description: The lease ledger: game-dollar rent, deposits, and the first-of-the-month rhythm every resident — hired characters included — lives under.

item.title: Every request knocks before it enters.
item.description: The request pipeline's screening contract: intent screening, human review for the gray zone, denies that always refund, and public attribution on everything.

item.title: How the block learned to look like the Mission.
item.description: The render history behind the neighborhood — what twenty-eight versions of sun, fog, and rooflines did to one San Francisco block.
